record.original_question: For a graph G, let ed(G) be the smallest integer k >= 1 such that every assignment of vectors p_1,...,p_n admits vectors q_1,...,q_n in R^k preserving the squared distances on all edges of G. Let the suspension of G be the graph obtained by adding one new vertex adjacent to every vertex of G. Is ed(suspension(G)) <= ed(G) + 1, equivalently ed(suspension(G)) = ed(G) + 1 given the known reverse inequality?

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Determine the validity of the inequality ed(suspension G) <= ed(G) + 1, relating the Euclidean dimension of a graph G and of its suspension.

Given a graph G, its Euclidean dimension is the graph parameter ed(G) which is defined as the smallest integer k >= 1 such that, for every family of vectors p1,...,pn, there exists another family of vectors q1,...,qn in Rk satisfying squared edge distances. The suspension graph is obtained from G by adding to it a new node and making it adjacent to all the nodes of G.
Thus our first problem asks whether the converse inequality holds or, equivalently, whether it is true that ed(suspension G) = ed(G) + 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite simple graph $G=(V,E)$ on $n$ vertices, define the Euclidean dimension $\mathrm{ed}(G)$ to be the smallest integer $k\ge 1$ with the following property: for every assignment of vectors $p_1,\ldots,p_n$ (in any Euclidean space) to the vertices of $G$, there exist vectors $q_1,\ldots,q_n\in\mathbb{R}^k$ such that $\|q_i-q_j\|^2=\|p_i-p_j\|^2$ for every edge $\{i,j\}\in E$. The suspension of $G$, denoted $
abla G$, is the graph obtained from $G$ by adding a new vertex adjacent to all vertices of $G$. It is known that $\mathrm{ed}(
abla G)\ge \mathrm{ed}(G)+1$. Determine whether the converse inequality
$$\mathrm{ed}(
abla G)\le \mathrm{ed}(G)+1$$
holds for every graph $G$; equivalently, decide whether $\mathrm{ed}(
abla G)=\mathrm{ed}(G)+1$ for every graph $G$.
